# [CS018] HTTP Server Without Read Timeouts (http-server-missing-timeout)

An HTTP server is started without ReadHeaderTimeout or ReadTimeout.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | HIGH |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-400](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/400.html) |
| **OWASP** | A02:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

http.ListenAndServe and a Server without read timeouts keep connections open for clients that send headers byte by byte (Slowloris), so a few hosts can exhaust file descriptors and goroutines.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
http.ListenAndServe(":8080", mux)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
srv := &http.Server{
	Addr:              ":8080",
	Handler:           mux,
	ReadHeaderTimeout: 5 * time.Second,
	ReadTimeout:       30 * time.Second,
	IdleTimeout:       2 * time.Minute,
}
_ = srv.ListenAndServe()
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [http-server-missing-timeout]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    http-server-missing-timeout: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore http-server-missing-timeout -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** http-server-missing-timeout
```
